profiles.model: اِسْمُهُ بِلَالٌ، وَعُمْرُهُ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً. هُوَ بَاكِسْتَانِيٌّ، وَيَعِيشُ فِي لَنْدَنَ. يَتَكَلَّمُ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ وَالأُرْدِيَّةَ.

retrievalQuiz.q: Choose the greeting that means ‘peace be upon you’.?
retrievalQuiz.why: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ opens a respectful greeting exchange.

retrievalQuiz.q: Which phrase asks after a female listener?
retrievalQuiz.why: The final kasra in ـكِ addresses one female.

retrievalQuiz.q: Which line means ‘I am from Morocco’?
retrievalQuiz.why: مِنْ introduces origin: where someone is from.
أَسْكُنُ فِي introduces where someone lives.
The تـ prefix marks the third-person feminine form here.
The feminine noun and adjective both use feminine forms.

retrievalQuiz.q: Which phrase is a polite welcome to one female?
retrievalQuiz.why: تَفَضَّلِي addresses one female.

retrievalQuiz.q: Which sentence joins identity and language?
retrievalQuiz.why: The sentence uses a feminine nationality and the first-person language verb accurately.

vocabQuiz.why: مُجْتَمَعٌ can mean society or community.

vocabQuiz.q: Complete for a female speaker: أَنَا … بِثَقَافَتِي.

customsQuiz.q: What is the most accurate statement about greeting gestures?
a: They vary by person, family, setting and community.
Every Arab greeting includes a handshake.
customsQuiz.why: Greeting gestures vary; observe and follow the other person’s lead.

customsQuiz.q: Which Arabic phrase respectfully asks after the family?
customsQuiz.why: كَيْفَ الأَهْلُ؟ means ‘How is the family?’

customsQuiz.q: A guest declines tea. What is the respectful response?
a: Assume the guest dislikes the family.
customsQuiz.why: Hospitality includes respecting the guest’s preferences and boundaries.

customsQuiz.q: Which phrase is a warm welcome?
customsQuiz.why: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا is a warm welcome.

customsQuiz.q: What should a learner do when unsure about a greeting gesture?
a: Use words, observe and follow the other person’s lead.
Copy one rule for every country.
customsQuiz.why: Words plus attentive observation are respectful and adaptable.
فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ means ‘in some families’ and leaves room for variation.

customsQuiz.q: Which value can be shown through a careful greeting?
customsQuiz.why: A careful greeting can communicate respect.

customsQuiz.q: Which is the best cultural-learning habit?
a: Notice patterns while remembering that individuals differ.
Turn every observation into a universal rule.
Assume one country represents the whole Arab world.
customsQuiz.why: Cultural understanding needs both patterns and individual variation.

identityQuiz.q: Which list shows several possible layers of identity?
a: Name, family, language, place, belief and interests
identityQuiz.why: Identity can include many connected layers.
A female speaker uses فَخُورَةٌ and عَائِلَتِي means my family.

identityQuiz.q: A learner does not wish to discuss religion. What is appropriate?
a: Respect the choice and use another identity topic.
identityQuiz.why: Belief is personal; no learner should be required to disclose it.

identityQuiz.q: Which question asks one male about religion?
identityQuiz.why: ـكَ addresses one male; the question is for recognition and optional use only.

identityQuiz.q: Which question asks one female about religion?
identityQuiz.why: ـكِ addresses one female; personal disclosure remains optional.

a: أَنَا بَرِيطَانِيَّةٌ مِنْ عَائِلَةٍ سُورِيَّةٍ وَأَتَكَلَّمُ لُغَتَيْنِ.
identityQuiz.why: The sentence combines nationality, family background and language.

a: A person chooses which parts of identity to share.
identityQuiz.why: People control their own personal information and identity description.

listeningQuiz.why: Hanaa says her friend Maryam is visiting.

listeningQuiz.q: Which greeting does Hanaa use for Maryam?
listeningQuiz.why: She welcomes Maryam with أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا، تَفَضَّلِي.
She asks after the family: كَيْفَ الأَهْلُ؟

a: Greeting and hospitality customs differ from one family to another.
Every family follows exactly the same customs.
listeningQuiz.why: She explicitly says customs differ from one family to another.

finalQuiz.why: ثَقَافَةٌ means culture.
ضِيَافَةٌ means hospitality.
فَخُورَةٌ agrees with a female speaker or feminine noun.

finalQuiz.q: Which phrase asks after the family?
finalQuiz.why: كَيْفَ الأَهْلُ؟ asks how the family is.

finalQuiz.q: Which phrase avoids a universal claim?
finalQuiz.why: فِي بَعْضِ العَائِلَاتِ means ‘in some families’.

finalQuiz.q: What should you do when greeting customs are unclear?
a: Use respectful words, observe and follow the other person’s lead.
finalQuiz.why: Observation and choice protect respect and individual boundaries.

a: Identity may include family, language, place, belief and interests.
finalQuiz.why: Identity can have several layers and remains personal.

finalQuiz.q: How should a religion question be handled in this lesson?
a: As recognition/optional language, with no required personal disclosure
finalQuiz.why: Religion is sensitive personal information; disclosure is optional.

finalQuiz.q: What did Hanaa offer in the listening task?
finalQuiz.why: The transcript says tea and dates.

finalQuiz.q: What was Rami’s main point in the reading?
a: Respect matters more than one fixed greeting form.
Only Arabic may be spoken at home.
finalQuiz.why: Rami values respect over a particular gesture.
وَلَكِنْ means ‘but’ and introduces contrast.

finalQuiz.q: Which is the best final cultural statement?
a: Practices vary, so I describe evidence carefully and respect personal choice.
One family represents an entire country.
All Arabic-speaking communities share identical traditions.
finalQuiz.why: Careful evidence, variation and choice are the core cultural-learning principles.

cultureRounds.statement: Greeting gestures can vary by person, family, setting and community.
cultureRounds.why: This is respectful and accurate because it recognises variation.

cultureRounds.statement: Every Arab family serves coffee to every visitor.
cultureRounds.why: This needs more care. Some families serve coffee, tea, another drink or nothing; guests may also decline.

cultureRounds.statement: I prefer to greet with words rather than physical contact.
cultureRounds.why: This is a personal choice and should be respected.

cultureRounds.statement: One country represents all Arabic-speaking communities.
cultureRounds.why: The Arab world and Arabic-speaking communities are diverse; one example cannot represent everyone.

cultureRounds.statement: In some families, asking after relatives is part of a warm greeting.
cultureRounds.why: The phrase ‘in some families’ reports a pattern without making it universal.

cultureRounds.statement: A student must tell the class their religion.
cultureRounds.why: Religion is personal information. No learner should be required to disclose it.

cultureRounds.statement: A person can identify with more than one culture.
cultureRounds.why: Layered or mixed cultural identity is common and accurately described.

cultureRounds.statement: I will observe and follow the other person’s lead when I am unsure.
cultureRounds.why: This is a practical and respectful approach.

cultureRounds.statement: I do not drink tea, but I appreciate the offer.
cultureRounds.why: A guest may politely decline; hospitality includes respecting that choice.

cultureRounds.statement: I can know someone’s religion from their appearance.
cultureRounds.why: Appearance does not reliably reveal belief and assumptions can be harmful.

cultureRounds.statement: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ is one respectful Arabic greeting, alongside other appropriate greetings.
cultureRounds.why: This recognises the phrase’s importance without claiming it is the only possible greeting.

cultureRounds.statement: Our family has its own way of welcoming visitors.
cultureRounds.why: A family may describe its own practice without presenting it as a rule for others.

speakingProfiles.title: A Moroccan-British family in Birmingham
speakingProfiles.details: Greeting: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ · hospitality: mint tea · languages: Arabic and English · variation: some relatives shake hands; others use words only.
speakingProfiles.model: هَذِهِ عَائِلَةٌ مَغْرِبِيَّةٌ بَرِيطَانِيَّةٌ تَعِيشُ فِي بِرْمِنْغَامَ. يَقُولُونَ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ عِنْدَ اللِّقَاءِ، وَيُقَدِّمُونَ الشَّايَ لِلضُّيُوفِ. يَتَكَلَّمُونَ العَرَبِيَّةَ وَالإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ. بَعْضُ الأَقَارِبِ يُصَافِحُونَ، وَلَكِنَّ آخَرِينَ يُفَضِّلُونَ التَّحِيَّةَ بِالكَلِمَاتِ.

speakingProfiles.title: A Jordanian family welcoming a neighbour
speakingProfiles.details: Greeting: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا · hospitality: tea and dates · family question: كَيْفَ الأَهْلُ؟ · emphasis: guest choice is respected.
speakingProfiles.model: هَذِهِ عَائِلَةٌ أُرْدُنِيَّةٌ. عِنْدَمَا يَصِلُ الجَارُ يَقُولُونَ أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا وَيَسْأَلُونَ كَيْفَ الأَهْلُ؟ يُقَدِّمُونَ الشَّايَ وَالتَّمْرَ، وَلَكِنَّهُمْ يَحْتَرِمُونَ اِخْتِيَارَ الضَّيْفِ.

speakingProfiles.title: A multilingual Lebanese family in Manchester
speakingProfiles.details: Languages: Arabic, English and French · greeting varies by setting · identity combines family background and British life.
speakingProfiles.model: هَذِهِ عَائِلَةٌ لُبْنَانِيَّةٌ تَعِيشُ فِي مَانْشِسْتَرَ. يَتَكَلَّمُونَ ثَلَاثَ لُغَاتٍ. تَخْتَلِفُ التَّحِيَّةُ فِي البَيْتِ عَنِ المَدْرَسَةِ. هُوِيَّتُهُمْ تَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ ثَقَافَةِ العَائِلَةِ وَالحَيَاةِ فِي بَرِيطَانِيَا.

speakingProfiles.title: An Egyptian family at a large gathering
speakingProfiles.details: Greeting: warm verbal exchange · asks about health and family · hospitality: several optional drinks · practices differ by generation.
speakingProfiles.model: فِي هَذَا التَّجَمُّعِ تَرْحَبُ عَائِلَةٌ مِصْرِيَّةٌ بِالضُّيُوفِ. يَسْأَلُونَ عَنِ الصِّحَّةِ وَالعَائِلَةِ وَيُقَدِّمُونَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ مَشْرُوبٍ. تَخْتَلِفُ بَعْضُ العَادَاتِ بَيْنَ الأَجْيَالِ، وَلَكِنَّ الاِحْتِرَامَ مُهِمٌّ لِلْجَمِيعِ.

speakingProfiles.title: A Syrian-British student describing identity
speakingProfiles.details: Proud of family language and British school community · greets friends differently from older relatives · no personal belief disclosure required.
speakingProfiles.model: هَذَا طَالِبٌ سُورِيٌّ بَرِيطَانِيٌّ. هُوَ فَخُورٌ بِلُغَةِ عَائِلَتِهِ وَبِمُجْتَمَعِ مَدْرَسَتِهِ. تَحِيَّتُهُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِهِ قَصِيرَةٌ، وَلَكِنَّهُ يَسْأَلُ أَقَارِبَهُ الكِبَارَ عَنِ الصِّحَّةِ وَالأَهْلِ.

speakingProfiles.title: A fictional international Arabic club
speakingProfiles.details: Members come from several backgrounds · use Arabic greetings · bring different family customs · agree to ask before physical contact.
speakingProfiles.model: فِي نَادِي اللُّغَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ طُلَّابٌ مِنْ خَلْفِيَّاتٍ مُخْتَلِفَةٍ. يَسْتَعْمِلُونَ تَحِيَّاتٍ عَرَبِيَّةً، وَلِكُلِّ طَالِبٍ عَادَاتٌ عَائِلِيَّةٌ خَاصَّةٌ. يَتَّفِقُونَ عَلَى السُّؤَالِ وَالاِحْتِرَامِ قَبْلَ أَيِّ تَوَاصُلٍ جَسَدِيٍّ.

retrievalQuiz.why: اِسْمِي introduces the speaker’s own name.

retrievalQuiz.q: Which phrase gives the speaker’s age?
retrievalQuiz.why: عُمْرِي means ‘my age’, and سَنَةً completes the age phrase.

retrievalQuiz.q: Which sentence means ‘I am from Jordan’?
retrievalQuiz.why: مِنْ introduces origin: where someone is from.
أَسْكُنُ فِي introduces place of residence.

retrievalQuiz.q: A female student says ‘My nationality is Lebanese’. Choose the correct line.
retrievalQuiz.why: The female nationality adjective is لُبْنَانِيَّةٌ.
أَتَكَلَّمُ is the first-person form.

vocabQuiz.why: It asks where the person lives.

connectiveQuiz.why: وَ joins the two related personal facts.

connectiveQuiz.q: Which connective is best for ‘I speak Arabic, but my writing needs practice’?

connectiveQuiz.why: أَيْضًا adds the second language fact naturally.

connectiveQuiz.q: Which line gives a complete reason?

connectiveQuiz.q: Which connective should not be added without a following reason?
connectiveQuiz.why: لِأَنَّ must introduce a reason; it cannot stand alone.

connectiveQuiz.q: Which sequence is most logical for the writing process?
connectiveQuiz.why: The correct sentence uses ثُمَّ to order planning, writing and checking.

editQuiz.q: Which opening improves a bare list of facts?

editQuiz.q: Which revision joins name and age most clearly?
a: اِسْمِي عَلِيٌّ، وَعُمْرِي أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً.
editQuiz.why: The sentence contains both complete facts joined by وَ.
The nationality adjective agrees with the female speaker.

editQuiz.q: Which change adds useful detail rather than repetition?
editQuiz.why: The first line adds a different language skill and uses أَيْضًا.
The complete reason explains why the speaker likes drawing.

editQuiz.q: Which punctuation helps separate two connected facts?

A question mark after every sentence

editQuiz.q: Which closing completes the introduction politely?
editQuiz.why: The phrase thanks the listener and signals the end.
